label: Longest river systems
note: Approximate whole-system lengths. Sources differ on headwaters and measurement; the Nile–Amazon order is disputed. Country lists describe the course, not every country in the drainage basin.

entries.name: Nile
entries.route: East African headwaters → Lake Victoria / White Nile; Blue Nile from Ethiopia → Mediterranean Sea.
entries.detail: The White and Blue Nile meet at Khartoum. Tributaries and the basin extend beyond the countries on the main course.

entries.name: Amazon
entries.route: Andean headwaters in Peru → across northern Brazil → Atlantic Ocean.
entries.detail: The Amazon carries more water than any other river. Its longest headwater and total length remain debated.

entries.name: Yangtze
entries.route: Tibetan Plateau → central and eastern China → East China Sea.
entries.detail: China’s longest river is also called Chang Jiang.

entries.name: Mississippi–Missouri
entries.route: Rocky Mountain headwaters → Missouri → Mississippi → Gulf of Mexico.
entries.detail: This ranking measures the connected river system, not the Mississippi main stem alone.

entries.name: Yenisey–Angara
entries.route: Mongolian headwaters / Lake Baikal tributary system → Siberia → Kara Sea.
entries.detail: A connected system flowing north toward the Arctic Ocean.

coverage: Five longest river systems in this source’s convention.
